issues.legal_issue: Land occupied by persons asserting an independent right to remain after redemption of a mortgage is not in the proprietor’s khas possession under the statutory saving for land subject to a subsisting mortgage.
material_facts: The proprietors’ predecessors had mortgaged the land, and the mortgage was paid off and discharged in 1941.
The occupants had entered under a lease during the mortgage but, after redemption, refused to surrender possession and asserted occupancy rights of their own.
The proprietors claimed the occupants were trespassers, sought possession and mesne profits, and the occupants remained in possession when the estate vested in the State.
The appeal challenged the setting aside of the trial court’s possession decree following that vesting.
issues.conclusion: The land was not saved from vesting as land in the proprietors’ khas possession under the mortgage provision; the proprietors could not retain the decree for possession, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(k), 3(1), 4(a), and 6(1)(c) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, only land meeting the statutory conditions for khas possession is saved from vesting. Section 2(k) defines khas possession by reference to possession through the proprietor’s own cultivation or agricultural operations; section 6(1)(c) addresses land forming the subject matter of a subsisting mortgage on redemption of which the intermediary is entitled to recover khas possession. A mere right to possession is not itself khas possession. The court rejected the broad equation of constructive possession with khas possession suggested by Mahanth Sukhdeo Das v. Kashi Prasad Tiwari, AIR 1958 Pat. 630, insofar as it would treat a trespasser’s possession as the owner’s khas possession. The land here was occupied adversely in the occupants’ own right, and the mortgagor-mortgagee relationship did not subsist on the vesting date.

predicates.appeal_challenges_denial_of_possession_a: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the denial of a possession decree after statutory vesting of an estate.
predicates.estate_vested_in_state: The estate in which the land lies vested in the State under a statutory vesting process.
predicates.mortgage_was_discharged_before_vesting: The mortgage affecting the land had been paid off and discharged before the estate vested.
predicates.occupants_asserted_independent_right_to_: The persons occupying the land refused to surrender it and claimed a right to remain that they asserted against the proprietor.
predicates.occupants_held_possession_adversely_to_p: The occupants possessed the land in their own right rather than on behalf of, or derivatively from, the proprietor.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns possession after statutory vesting and the land was occupied by persons asserting their own adverse right after discharge of the mortgage, the proprietor cannot retain possession under the statutory saving.

issues.legal_issue: Occupants who entered through a mortgage-related tenancy but, after redemption, openly resist the proprietor’s claim and assert a right to remain possess in their own right rather than on behalf of the proprietor.
material_facts: The occupants entered the land as tenants during the mortgage.
After the proprietors redeemed the mortgage, the occupants resisted the proprietors’ entry and asserted occupancy rights against them.
The proprietors pleaded that the occupants’ continued possession was wrongful and sought mesne profits and recovery of possession.
The occupants’ possession continued after the mortgage was discharged.
issues.conclusion: The occupants’ possession was in their own right and adverse to the proprietors; it could not be treated as possession on behalf of the mortgagors or as possession derived from them.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle reflected in article 144 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908: possession initially held in a permissive or representative capacity may become adverse when an overt act or open claim renounces that capacity and asserts possession in one’s own right to the owner’s knowledge. The court said this applies a fortiori where the possessor is not the mortgagee but another person, such as a tenant, who resists the mortgagor’s claim and asserts an independent right. The authorities discussed concerning a mortgagee’s continued possession after redemption did not require a different result on these facts; the court did not treat the occupants as continuing to hold through the mortgagee or for the mortgagors.

predicates.proceeding_requires_determining_characte: The proceeding requires the court to determine whether occupants hold land on behalf of an owner or in their own right.
predicates.occupants_entered_during_mortgage: The occupants first entered the land as tenants while a mortgage affecting it was in force.
predicates.mortgage_was_redeemed: The owner paid off and discharged the mortgage.
predicates.occupants_openly_resisted_owner_and_clai: After the mortgage was discharged, the occupants resisted the owner’s demand for possession and asserted their own right to remain.

issues.definition: When occupants entered during a mortgage but openly resist the owner after redemption and claim the land in their own right, their possession is adverse rather than held on the owner’s behalf.
